title: Where each Zscaler product's logs go and how to get them out
aliases: where do i find this log
nss vs lss vs cloud nss

prose.text: Each product has its own way out. Find the product first, then the path.

rows: ZIA web, firewall, DNS, tunnel and the other ZIA log types
An NSS feed on VM-based NSS or Cloud NSS [[shared.nss.feeds]]
ZPA user activity, user status, App Connector, audit and other Private Access logs
A log receiver fed by App Connectors [[zpa.log-receivers.architecture]]
Kept on the device; collected by export, Report an Issue or Fetch Logs [[zcc.logging.collection]]
ZDX scores, alerts and device data
Cloud Connector session logs and Insights
Third-party firewall and proxy logs, inbound

prose.label: DLP and Sandbox.
prose.text: The web feed carries inline DLP and Sandbox fields: [[zia/web-log]], [[zia.logs.web-field-semantics:dlp-rule-fields]], [[zia.logs.web-field-semantics:malwarecat-sandbox]]. Endpoint DLP, Email DLP and Sandbox Verdict logs also have feeds of their own: [[shared.nss.feeds:feed-log-types]].

prose.label: Delivery differs by path.
prose.text: NSS recovery and retry rules are in [[shared.nss.reliability]]. ZPA's stream drops logs from a connection loss except for a short retransmit and audit logs: [[zpa.app-connectors.health:lss-retransmit-limits]], with retention in [[zpa.log-receivers.delivery]].

prose.label: LSS is a separate path.
prose.text: TLS between App Connector and receiver is optional, not required: [[zpa.log-receivers.tls:mutual-tls-optional]]. Whether LSS shares the Nanolog store with NSS is not stated {{gap:lss-store}}.

prose.label: Client Connector logs are not a SIEM stream.
prose.text: What users can export and when it is readable is [[zcc.logging.user-access]]; whether the client log records individual transactions is open in [[zcc.logs.client-log]].

prose.label: Landing in a SIEM.
prose.text: Which log type to look for and how it tends to be named in a SIEM: [[shared.siem-mapping]]. Joining records across streams: [[shared.log-correlation]].

checks.do: For a per-URL allow or block decision, read the ZIA web log and its rule fields rather than the Client Connector log.
For a gap in a SIEM, which path the log type takes before applying a recovery rule: NSS or LSS.

lss-store.title: Whether LSS reads from the Nanolog
lss-store.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "LSS ... is architecturally distinct from NSS; it does not go through the Nanolog cluster." The help says NSS streams from the Zscaler Nanolog and that LSS resides in the Zero Trust Exchange and starts its stream through a Public Service Edge; it does not say where Private Access logs are stored before streaming.
lss-store.blocks: reasoning about whether a Nanolog outage affects ZPA log streaming
